Subject: Hosted→Dedicated migration — initial bridge & commit framework

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — great to hear more about Optima's inference mix for clinical summarization and real-time triage. Per our conversation I put together an initial framework for the hosted→dedicated migration economics so your finance/procurement team can review quickly. High-level proposal below; I attached a simple conversion schedule and a draft SLA you can share with Procurement.

Summary (proposal):
- Conversion credit: 3 months of your trailing hosted spend (max $120k) applied as a dollar-for-dollar credit against the first 6 months of the Dedicated commit. Credits vest monthly as committed usage ramps.
- Bridge months: 2 complimentary bridge months (Dedicated capacity with limited throughput quota) to reduce downtime risk during onboarding.
- Commit ladder: 12-month reserved commit with front-loaded ramp schedule: 25% commit Month 1–2, 50% Month 3–4, 100% Month 5 onward.
- GPU pool sizing: initial target 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (NVIDIA A100 80GB or equivalent share); expected steady-state throughput ~1,200 requests/min (approx. 100 rps) at median request size.
- Throughput guarantee & SLA: p95 latency target 200ms for small chat requests, throughput SLO mapped to pooled concurrency. Failure to meet committed throughput triggers pro-rated credits. Details in attached SLA draft.

Ask: Can Procurement confirm (1) whether credits need to be a separate invoice line or can be applied on month 1 allocation, and (2) any legal procurement constraints on bridging discounts (we can put the credit mechanics in DocuSign).

I've attached: Optima_RI_Conversion_Schedule.xlsx (numbers by month) and Dedicated_SLA_Draft.pdf.

If that looks reasonable I can loop in Marissa (sales leader) and Karthik (solutions infra) to finalize sizing and DocuSign.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Steph — quick internal note before we respond to Optima's procurement asks:

- Line-item credits are ok from our billing side; we should express the conversion credit as a one-time negative invoice applied against month 1 charges up to the $120k cap. Legal may want the exact wording; Marissa can sign off.
- Bridge months: proposal should guarantee a baseline throughput of 60% of the committed concurrency per bridge month (we'll explicitly carve out onboarding quota for tests). If Optima needs full production parity we should offer 1 paid bridge month + 1 complimentary testing month instead to protect capacity.
- GPU sizing: work with Karthik to run a short perf estimate. For planning numbers: 4x A100 (80GB) with our optimizations typically yields ~7500 tokens/sec aggregate (KV cache warm) and p95 latency ~220–260ms at 2k token windows for our medium-sized LLM family. If Optima needs lower latencies at 2k tokens we should size to 6 GPUs or enable quantized variants.

I'll let Karthik reply with the performance numbers. Also recommend we offer a 3-tier commit ladder discount: 5% for 12–24k GPU-hours/month, 10% for 24–48k, 15% for >48k — that gives Procurement levers.

-Ben

Steph / Ben — performance numbers and sizing notes below (keeping Optima's 2k token window in mind):

- 4x A100-80GB (our stack w/ optimized kernels + continuous batching):
  * Steady-state aggregate throughput: ~7,200 tokens/sec (warm cache)
  * Typical median request p50 latency: ~140ms for 2k tokens (streaming off), p95: ~310ms at peak concurrency
  * Expected sustained qps: ~90–110 rps depending on batching and request mix

- For tighter p95 targets (<=250ms at 2k tokens) we recommend 6x A100-equivalents or enabling lower-precision quantized variant (nv-int8) which reduces p95 by ~20–30% but may need evals for quality.

- Bridge months behaviour: we can provision the dedicated pool with an onboarding soft cap equal to 60% of your planned steady-state concurrency; during the two complimentary months we will allow staged ramp tests up to 100% for 48 hours if scheduled in advance. Any sustained production traffic beyond the soft cap is subject to overage charges.

I can produce a short perf appendix to include in the SLA draft.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Sam / Procurement team — thanks for the quick review and questions. Per internal alignment here is a revised, procurement-friendly offer: 

1) Conversion credit: expressed as a one-line negative invoice item applied to month 1 charges, cap $120,000. Credit vests monthly over the first 6 months as committed usage hits ramp milestones in the attached schedule.
2) Bridge months: 2 bridge months; baseline provisioning = 60% steady-state throughput. Optima can schedule up to 2 x 24-hour full-capacity validation windows during the bridge period (we'll pre-book with infra).
3) GPU sizing options:
   - Option A (baseline): 4x A100-equivalent GPUs — expected p95 ~310ms at 2k tokens, aggregate ~7.2k tokens/sec.
   - Option B (performance): 6x A100-equivalent GPUs — expected p95 <=250ms at 2k tokens.
   - Option C (cost-optimized): 4x quantized instances (nv-int8) — ~20% lower latency and ~30% lower cost but requires evaluation on your models.
4) Commit ladder & discounts: 12-month commit with staged ramp (25%→50%→100%) and discount tiers we discussed (5/10/15%). We will outline GPU-hour ranges in the attached spreadsheet.

Next steps: (a) Procurement — confirm whether you require a PO before DocuSign, (b) Sam — pick A/B/C for the first 3 months so we can size the pool, (c) I will send a DocuSign-ready agreement once we have the PO or confirmation on line-item credit.

If that works I'll issue the DocuSign and update the SLA appendix with Karthik's perf numbers.

Best,
